artifacts.detail: Restorable only from an off-host backup (REC-01, REC-02). The file is deleted on container restart/recreate and no key material exists anywhere else. Without a backup the identity is unrecoverable (REC-03, drill DR-05).

Restorable from an off-host backup, or regenerable from the master key with a higher sequence (REC-07, drill DR-04). A restored token with a regressed sequence is silently stale (REC-08, drill DR-03).
artifacts.location: [validator_token] in postfiatd.cfg; source of truth is GitHub Secrets in the deploy workflow

artifacts.detail: Comes back only with validator-keys.json (REC-07). A seed-only restore resets the sequence to 0 (REC-04), which peers dispose as stale (REC-08, drill DR-03). There is no out-of-band sequence record in the tree.
artifacts.location: Stored in validator-keys.json; not stored anywhere else

artifacts.detail: Restorable from an off-host backup, or regenerable from the documented example config except for the token/seed sections (REC-12). The deploy workflow deletes the config volume on every redeploy and re-injects the token from GitHub Secrets (REC-17, REC-18).

Restorable from backup, or re-fetchable from the publisher site (REC-13). The mainnet file trusts exactly one publisher key and a testnet URL (REC-14); with one publisher the threshold is 1 (REC-15). A wrong list silently un-trusts the validator (drill DR-08).
artifacts.location: validators.txt in the config directory; fetched from the publisher site

artifacts.detail: No backup artifact in the tree covers ledger data (REC-29). The node must re-acquire ledger state from peers via ledger replay (REC-24); how long that takes is UNTESTABLE in the lab (drill DR-09). A snapshot whose hash matches no validated ledger is unusable.

Holds manifests; the hotfix doc orders a backup before any destructive restart and forbids deleting wallet.db as a recovery procedure (REC-23). It is not part of the documented validator backup (REC-29), so it is usually lost with the host.
